name: module-error-variable-test-718d21c637/module-error-variable-negative-e.bal
spec_references: ## Module-level declarations: [Annotation declarations and attachments](https://ballerina.io/spec/lang/master/#section_9.1); Supports source-only, runtime, marker and repeated annotations
reason: The case checks rejection of invalid module error-variable declarations: duplicate bindings, isolated/configurable qualifiers on non-simple bindings, an annotation attached to a disallowed declaration, references to subsequently bound module variables, incompatible nested error/mapping bindings, and missing required error-detail fields. Module variable declarations, type definitions, annotations, error constructors, and the associated type checking are supported without a restriction excluding error binding patterns. The wildcard-only restriction is explicitly for destructuring assignment statements; these are variable declarations. The illegal qualifiers and attachments are negative assertions within supported declaration grammar, not evidence of an essential unsupported feature.
test_design_notes: Compile-negative source with inline @error markers; no runtime behavior is asserted.
Do not apply the destructuring-assignment restriction to module variable binding patterns.
